units.translation: someone, said of a definite person whom one does not wish to name more explicitly
some, joined with substantives or adjectives
some, added to common nouns to indicate a certain likeness
some, with adjectives and pronouns to embrace a whole class
in some way, to some extent

The scholiast reads τί ἐκ [what from], interpreting: τί δεῖ ὑπονοῆσαι ἐκ τούτων ἢ πένθη καὶ συμφοράς; [what must be inferred from these things except griefs and misfortunes?]. The hiatus τί ἐκ [what from] is suspect. For although the tragedians sometimes said τί οὖν [what then] in trimeters, about which will be said below, nevertheless it is not likely that Aeschylus wrote τί ἐκ [what from] in a melic song, especially since the antistrophic verse 368 begins with the long syllable παγκλαύτων [all-lamenting], on the evidence of which Kayser conjectured ποῖ ἐκ τῶνδ᾽ [whither from these things].
where the sense requires ἢ γάρ τι πιστόν ἐστι [or is there anything trustworthy], which Karsten restored
Thus it seems to have been rightly corrected for ποίου φρονήματος [of what kind of thought], as was said under ποῖος
i.e. what do you seek? whom?
On the contraction of τί ποτε [what ever] into τίπτε [why] it was said above p. 301 b.
Thus Abreschius for τιμήν [honor].
But at line 313 τί οὖν ὁ Δῖος πόρτις εὔχεται βοός; [what then does the calf of Zeus pray for from the cow?] now from Stanley's emendation is read τίς οὖν [who then].
where Meineke Philol. vol. 19 p. 232 reads τί ἂν γενοίμαν [what would I become?]
Thus (or ἢ τίνος [or of whom]) some copies have for οὔτινος [of no one], which is in M.
Thus I corrected for μήποτε θεὸς μήτε τις ανος [never a god nor any man] (i.e. ἄνθρωπος [man], changed by a corrector to ἄλλος [another]).
i.e. Aegisthus.

But at Sept. 402 ή ἄνοιά τινι [the folly of someone] is an interpolation of an interpolator when the poet's words had fallen out, which seem to have been οἷα πείσεται [what things he will suffer]: about which I have spoken in the annotation.
where Wellauer reads δίψησις [thirst].
where I emended to πανουργίας πλέως [full of villainy].
where I deleted γε [at least].
corrupt from πυρδαῆτιν [fire-brand].
Thus Turnebus for πόσον δή [how much then].
Who of the gods is so stout-hearted?
Who is not vexed?
Who then is the helmsman of necessity?
Whom shall I say I see here?
Who are you? Who indeed addresses me so truly?
By whom, O queen, will the scepters be plundered?
Who then is the one who will release you?
Who will save? Who will come to aid?
Whom will you oppose to him? Who is surety to guard the gates of Proetus?
Who will stand against him? Who, without trembling, will await the boastful man?
Who could provide purifications? Who could wash him?
For which of men did they admire so much?
Men—which ones?
Who then could persuade these things?
Who is the lord with swift foot of easy-flying leap?
And what shepherd is in charge?
Who has not died? Whom of the leaders shall we mourn?
Who began the rites?
And who of my children commanded the army there?
And what speed of messengers could arrive here?
Who knows?
Who is this child?
Who except the gods is without pain for all the time of life?
Who ever named it?
And who will quench it?
Who could call back the black blood?
Who of mortals could ever pray for it?
Who cries out a blow, wounded to the death?
Who will bear witness?
Who will bury him? Who will lament?
Who could cast out the accursed offspring from the house?
